questions.question: Circle-line intersections followed by a tangent
questions.subtopic: Circle-line intersections followed by a tangent
questions.prompt: The circle C has equation (x−1)²+(y−2)²=25. The line L has equation 4y=3x+5. (a) Find the centre and radius of C. (b) Calculate the exact coordinates of both points where L meets C. (c) At the point with larger x-coordinate, find an equation of the tangent to C in the form ax+by=c. [8 marks]
markPoints: Centre of C is (1,2), with radius 5.
Substitutes y=(3x+5)/4 into the circle, or uses an equivalent exact line-and-circle method.
Simplifies the intersection condition to x²−2x−15=0, or to (x−1)²=16.
Finds x=−3 and x=5.
Obtains corresponding y values −1 and 5, identifying intersection points (−3,−1) and (5,5).
At P=(5,5) calculates radius vector CP=(4,3) or radius gradient 3/4.
Uses perpendicularity of tangent to radius to get tangent slope −4/3.
Obtains tangent equation 4x+3y=35, or an exactly equivalent equation.
questions.modelAnswer: Centre (1,2), radius 5. Substitute y=(3x+5)/4 into (x−1)²+(y−2)²=25: (x−1)²+((3x−3)/4)²=25, so (25/16)(x−1)²=25, hence (x−1)²=16 and x=−3,5. From y=(3x+5)/4 the intersections are (−3,−1) and (5,5). At P=(5,5), CP=(4,3), radius slope 3/4, tangent slope −4/3. y−5=−(4/3)(x−5), giving 4x+3y=35.

questions.question: Circle from a diameter, perpendicular lines and tangent
questions.subtopic: Circle from a diameter, perpendicular lines and tangent
questions.prompt: A circle has diameter endpoints A=(−2,1) and B=(6,5). (a) Determine the centre and radius and give its equation. (b) Verify that C=(4,−1) lies on the circle. (c) Prove that angle ACB is a right angle using gradients, then find the tangent at C in the form ax+by+c=0. [8 marks]
markPoints: Centre is midpoint of AB: (2,3).
Radius is half |AB|, namely √20=2√5.
Circle equation (x−2)²+(y−3)²=20.
Checks (4−2)²+(−1−3)²=4+16=20, so C lies on the circle.
Gradient of CA is (1−(−1))/(−2−4)=−1/3.
Gradient of CB is (5−(−1))/(6−4)=3; product (−1/3)×3=−1 gives a right angle.
Radius from centre to C has slope −4/2=−2; the tangent's gradient is +1/2.
Tangent at C is y+1=(1/2)(x−4), equivalently x−2y−6=0.
questions.modelAnswer: Midpoint of diameter AB is ((−2+6)/2,(1+5)/2)=(2,3). |AB|=√(8²+4²)=√80, so radius=√20. Circle (x−2)²+(y−3)²=20. At C=(4,−1), 2²+(−4)²=20. Gradient CA=(1+1)/(−2−4)=−1/3; gradient CB=(5+1)/(6−4)=3. Their product is −1, giving angle ACB=90°. Centre-to-C slope (−1−3)/(4−2)=−2, so tangent slope 1/2. Through C: y+1=(x−4)/2, hence x−2y−6=0.

questions.question: Determine an unknown collinear position vector
questions.subtopic: Determine an unknown collinear position vector
questions.prompt: Three distinct points have position vectors A=(−1,4), B=(5,−2) and C=(k,2k−6). Given that A, B and C are collinear, (a) find k, (b) give the ratio AC:CB in simplest form, (c) calculate the exact distance AC and (d) find a unit vector pointing from A to B. Show vector working rather than assuming a diagram is to scale. [7 marks]
markPoints: Calculates AB=B−A=(6,−6).
Calculates AC=C−A=(k+1,2k−10).
Uses collinearity, for example equal component ratios or line y=−x+3, to obtain 2k−10=−(k+1).
Solves 3k=9, so k=3 and C=(3,0).
Finds AC=(4,−4) and CB=(2,−2), so the ratio AC:CB=2:1.
Calculates |AC|=√(4²+(−4)²)=4√2.
Obtains unit vector AB/|AB|=(1/√2,−1/√2) (or equivalent).
questions.modelAnswer: AB=(5−(−1),−2−4)=(6,−6). AC=(k+1,(2k−6)−4)=(k+1,2k−10). Because AB has equal and opposite components, AC must satisfy 2k−10=−(k+1), so 3k=9 and k=3. C=(3,0), AC=(4,−4), CB=(2,−2), and AC:CB=2:1. |AC|=√32=4√2. |AB|=6√2 and the unit vector AB/|AB|=(1/√2,−1/√2).
